$comment: DRAFT — not a shipped contract. Authority: docs/01-CONTRACT.md §12 (which DECLINES to define a Markdown projection, on Workbench rule 8) and docs/history/10-V11-SCOPE.md §4 (the four laws this artifact is built to satisfy instead). Written from crates/ethos-parser-core/src/markdown.rs. A PROJECTION, not the record: the representation is the evidence, this is derived from it and is deliberately lossy, and `coverage` is where it says how. The id was a https://ethos.dev/ URL at v1.1-S1, which implied a published, resolvable schema location that does not exist; it now uses the same urn scheme as every sibling here.
title: ethos.markdown.v1
description: A Markdown projection of a DocumentRepresentation, carried TOGETHER WITH the Anchor Map that inverts it back to representation nodes, a coverage census of every source character that did not reach it, and a second census of the structure GFM could not carry (v1.1-S1, S2, S3). docs/01-CONTRACT.md §12 declines to define a Markdown projection on Workbench rule 8 — a projection sitting between what a retriever ranks and what a citation binds is where a locator dies silently — and the parity checklist's O8 records that the rule PREFERS no projection at all to one without the map. This artifact exists because the map makes that objection payable, not because it lapsed. The consumer's rule is one line: a quote that touches a `syntax` byte is not invertible.

parser_version.description: The engine build that produced this artifact.

profile_sha256.description: Hash of the pinned configuration profile. Two artifacts are comparable if and only if this matches — and since v1.1-S1 the profile carries `markdown_rule`, so a run under a different projection rule is correctly non-comparable.

source_sha256.description: Digest of the original source bytes, carried through from the representation.

representation_sha256.description: Digest of the representation this projects. The binding that makes the map checkable: without it, a map could name node ids from a different parse of a different file and read exactly the same.

markdown_rule.description: Version id of the projection rule. `markdown-blocks-v2` (v1.1-S3) emits block structure: a GFM table for every table on the representation, a list item for every run the structure tree places in an `/L`, and headings taken only from the tree — never from a font size, a bullet glyph or a hanging indent (checklist L29 is REFUSE) — plus one export-only cosmetic, closing up a word the page broke across a line. It supersedes `markdown-blocks-v1`, which left the hyphen and the paragraph break where they were, and `markdown-linear-v1`, which emitted a table's cell runs as consecutive paragraphs with no grid around them. A document comes out differently under each, which is what a rule id on the profile is for. The cosmetic never touches the representation: both halves stay in the record with the hyphen verbatim, the joined bytes are one `source` segment naming both runs, and the removed hyphen is counted in `coverage.dropped` under `hyphenation-rejoin-dropped-v1`.

markdown.description: The Markdown. NEVER emitted without `anchor_map`: they are fields of one artifact rather than two files, because a companion file is a thing a pipeline strips and a field is not.

anchor_map.description: The map from `markdown` bytes back to evidence. Its segments TOTAL-TILE the string: sorted, contiguous, no overlap, no gap, covering 0..len(markdown) exactly. A map with a hole is worse than no map, because the hole is exactly where an unquotable byte hides — so an incomplete map is a hard error on both construction and parse, never a warning.

kind.description: TWO values, deliberately. `source` inverts to canonical node text; `syntax` is markup the exporter invented. There is no third — a 'probably source' would be the confidence field docs/01-CONTRACT.md §9 forbids, and would put the consumer back to guessing whether a quote is citable.

start.description: First UTF-8 BYTE offset into `markdown`, inclusive. Bytes rather than characters, and the description says so: every language's slice takes one or the other, and saying which is the difference between a map and a hint.

node_ids.description: The representation nodes these bytes came from, in emission order. Present on `source` and ABSENT on `syntax`, because syntax came from no node. Never a newly minted id: a projection that invented identifiers would be a second record of one document, and two records drift.

coverage.description: A census, not a summary. `source_chars_emitted + source_chars_dropped == source_chars_in_representation`, asserted in CI on real fixtures. Counted in CHARACTERS of node text, because the thing being conserved is the text the representation offered.

source_chars_in_representation.description: Sum of the character count of every node's text in the representation — the RAW text, not its normalization, so that whitespace the projection collapsed is visible as a bucket rather than hidden by moving the denominator.

source_chars_emitted.description: Characters that landed in a `source` segment.

source_chars_dropped.description: Characters that did not, summed over `dropped`.

dropped.description: Where the dropped characters went, by named class, sorted by code. Checklist A14: if something is removed, the artifact says so AND says how much. 'Some content was omitted' is not a disclosure; `annotation-text-not-projected-v1: 37` is.

structural_erasures.description: Structure the projection FLATTENED, by named class, sorted by code (v1.1-S2). A second census beside the character one, and separate from it deliberately: a merged cell's text is emitted in full, so nothing is dropped and a `tables-flattened` character bucket would read `0` — which is A14's own example of a disclosure that discloses nothing. What a merge costs is SLOTS, and what GFM's delimiter row costs is a header claim the document never made; neither is a number of characters. Empty means nothing was flattened, which is why it is a required key rather than an optional one.

code.description: `gfm-span-slots-unrepresentable-v1` — slots a merged cell covered that GFM cannot say it covered, `rowspan × colspan - 1` summed over the table's cells. `gfm-row-zero-separator-v1` — once per GFM table, because the delimiter row makes row 0 a header on every renderer and no detector reads `/TH`. `gfm-cell-run-claimed-twice-v1` — a run two cells both claimed, emitted under the first so that one node's characters are not counted twice. `gfm-cell-not-placed-v1` — a cell outside the declared grid or on a taken slot; its runs still project, as paragraphs. `gfm-table-not-projected-v1` — a table with zero rows or columns. `gfm-list-item-run-joins-v1` — a body run appended to an already-open list item, which is the one boundary a role path cannot settle. `mcid-run-joins-v1` — two runs the document placed in one marked-content sequence, emitted as one block, so the boundary between them is gone. `baseline-run-joins-abutted-v1` and `baseline-run-joins-spaced-v1` — the same erasure with no declaration behind it: two runs drawn as the next ink along one baseline, joined on this engine's geometry rather than the producer's word. The two are counted apart because the abutted form asserts one word and the spaced form only reproduces a space the page drew.

count.description: How many. Never a severity and never a ratio (docs/01-CONTRACT.md §9). Only non-zero classes appear: a list of codes all reading `0` is the disclosure-shaped noise a reader learns to skip, and every code is documented here whether or not a document trips it.
